title: Telemetry Handoff Gateway + Runbook Synthesizer for PagerDuty/Slack
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight 'handoff gateway' that transforms observability events into compact, actionable incident packets for PagerDuty and Slack, and synthesizes a first-draft runbook/postmortem seed. Goal is to reduce time-to-triage by providing contextual spans, related traces, metric slices, and a templated runbook attached to PD incidents and Slack threads.
acceptance_criteria: 1) PD incidents created by the gateway include: short summary, three high-confidence top spans, a condensed timeline (timestamps + span ids), and 1 link to the full trace in Console. 2) Slack incident posts render a concise card with action buttons (Acknowledge, Assign, Open Runbook). 3) Running for 7 days on canary traffic shows MTTR improvement signal or no regression, and no PII leaks in attachments. 4) Feature flag and rate controls exist; rollbacks are tested.
design_notes: Architecture: the gateway will subscribe to observability events from the telemetry bus (Kafka). For sampled high-severity signals it will: (a) fetch linked traces via trace-service API, (b) extract top spans using weighted-duration + error-score heuristic, (c) assemble a minimal JSON incident packet that includes metric-snapshot, log-excerpt (pre-defined regex redact), and runbook template filled with detected issue class. We will use a thin enrichment cache to avoid repeated trace fetches. PD integration via Events V2 with dedup keys; Slack via incoming webhook + Block Kit. Privacy: redaction rules applied with a redact-policy engine; security review required. Fall back to anonymized summary when traces are unavailable.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: prototype gateway service (canary mode, 5% of alerts) with PD event creation and Slack card posting. Phase 2: add runbook synthesizer using rule mapping + prompt-based template filler (local templates only, no external LLM calls). Phase 3: observability, SLOs, and rollout to 100% with opt-in configuration for projects. Feature flag gating and traffic percent controls via ops-config service.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dev deployment to staging. 2) Canary: enable for 10 internal teams (5% traffic) for 2 weeks. 3) Validate QA checklist (see testing_plan). 4) Ramp to 25% for 1 week; monitor PD noise and false-positive rate. 5) Full rollout with announcement and update to oncall runbooks. Rollback: disable feature flag; send TTR alert to #oncall-ops.
testing_plan: Unit tests for packet assembly, integration tests for PD and Slack endpoints (vcr-like fixtures), privacy fuzz tests to assert redaction rules, end-to-end test that simulates spike and verifies PD incident and Slack card contents, canary validation tests comparing MTTR and PD acknowledgment latency pre/post. Load test the gateway at expected peak alert fanout (x1000/min).
metrics_to_track: PD incident creation rate, duplicate incident rate (dedupe key collisions), Slack card click-through (open runbook), MTTR for canary teams, false-positive signal rate, gateway error rate, trace-fetch latency, redaction failure counts.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: overloading PD with noisy incidents. Mitigation: build conservative severity filters, backoff and batching. Risk: PII leakage. Mitigation: redact-policy enforced with audit logs and a pre-release privacy sweep. Risk: trace-service cost due to fetching full traces. Mitigation: cache top-span extracts and limit fetch frequency with TTL and sampling heuristics.
privacy_considerations: All extracted log snippets will run through redact-policy; by default we mask email-like tokens, IPs, and long hex strings. Customers can opt-out of trace attachment for private deployments. Audit log will record every generated incident packet for 30 days as part of compliance.
